implementation: Cooperative256-thread CTAs coalesce packed two-BF16 global loads into padded LDS K64 tiles. Two matrix fragments per wave cover64x64 or128x32 output cells. A64x64 register-prefetch variant loads the next K64 before its matrix work. Operand eligibility is immutable and cached, invalid or out-of-range rows are zeroed, and every lane reaches both retirement/publication barriers. Independently two-byte-skewed pointers use ordinary four-byte memcpy without stronger alignment promises. The original explicit zero-C signed/absolute K16 matrix operations, ascending FP32 group additions, C64 center/error recurrence with2^-19 coefficient, selection and full staged2 replay are unchanged.
correctness_scope: Every generated output is checked against independent CPU original K16 arithmetic. Every captured output is checked against external GB10 BF16 projection references and canonical full GPU original arithmetic, with256 independent CPU full dots per captured operator. Every warmup and timed sample compares all raw centers/errors to the scalar control, complete unique candidate membership, raw selected outputs, unselected output identity, error-envelope coverage, all prepared words/eligibility flags, immutable sources, guards and unused candidate tails. Candidate array order is not required to agree. The native error coefficient remains a conditional hardware model; tests do not prove a universal envelope.
timing_scope: Same-executable original scalar/vector controls and three shared-memory variants. One warmup and three rotated complete host-clock samples per captured shape. Clocks include prepare_rows, eligibility, matrix production, compaction, completed GPU synchronization, candidate count readback and all selected original replay. Prefix samples contain everything before replay, including count readback. Allocations, reset, reference computation and all validation are outside clocks. No model is loaded or token generated; these are q8192 operator shapes using7169 captured inputs plus1023 repeated rows. OUT has a full8192 GB10 operator reference; QKV repeats matching reference rows. No hardware occupancy or power inference is established.

code_object_metadata.scope: Static AMDGPU code-object metadata, not measured occupancy or pipeline behavior.

decision.decision: Keep all shared-memory variants isolated. They preserve every tested C64 center, envelope, candidate and raw replay result but lose to the same-executable vector-load control for both q8192 operators. OUT best shared96.3518ms versus vector93.6715ms; QKV best shared162.2570ms versus vector151.6550ms. No product dispatcher, package or acceptance change.
decision.next_step: Investigate the per-C64 error recurrence and repeated canonical arithmetic guards as a broader common-producer cost, rather than further LDS tile tuning. Prove restricted arithmetic domains before removing any guards; compare complete operators and the full GB10 boundary if a candidate is integrated.
decision.evidence_limits: Static VGPR counts94 for vector and206/227/214 for shared variants show larger compiled register requirements but do not establish measured occupancy or the cause of timings. Existing retained QKV uses a different producer and fewer candidates; this C64 comparison cannot qualify a QKV replacement. No real model tokens, TTFT or retained performance were measured.
